return_value: 1 when some file in the brief overlaps the range, 0 when none does; one find-arm sub-case (index in range, null range-end) returns the flag value itself instead of 1

semantics.compare: every comparison goes through one of the two routes in callees_by_contract, chosen per call by comparing the comparator's vtable slot +0xd0 against 0x5d48410 (the scan arms and the null-start arm load the guard as the immediate 0x5d48410; the find arm's second phase loads it from the relocated global at 0x64ecfb0, whose R_X86_64_RELATIVE addend is 0x5d48410)
semantics.find_arm: flag != 0. If the range start is null the index is 0 and neither the builder nor the find runs. Otherwise the record {range-start.data, range-start.length, packed = -8, tag = 0x16} is built into a std::string by the builder, the find helper is called with (comparator holder, brief, pointer to the string's (data, size) pair), the string is disposed, and the find result is taken at 32 bits zero-extended. If the index is not below the brief count (unsigned) the result is 0. Else if the range end is null the result is the flag value. Else the single file at that index is tested: compare(range end, file key A); the result is 1 when that comparison is >= 0 (computed as (not result) >> 31) and 0 when it is < 0
semantics.null_start_arm: flag == 0, count > 0, range start null. If the range end is also null the result is 1 at once. Otherwise the files are scanned in order and the result is 1 at the first file whose key A compares <= the range end (compare(range end, key A) >= 0); if no file qualifies the result is 0
semantics.scan_arm: flag == 0. A brief count of 0 returns 0 before any other test. With a non-null range start the files are scanned in order (count and array base re-read each iteration): a file is skipped while compare(range start, file key B) > 0; at the first file with compare <= 0 the file is a candidate -- a null range end returns 1 at once, otherwise compare(range end, file key A) >= 0 returns 1 and a negative result resumes the scan at the next file. Exhausting the array returns 0
